title: Fix: Allowed memory size exhausted - large loops and fetchAll
answer: The script used more memory than the limit allows, usually by loading a whole table with fetchAll or building a giant string in a loop. Process rows one at a time, unset large variables when done, and raise the limit only after fixing the cause. Raising the limit alone just delays the same crash.
pitfall: Setting memory_limit to -1 in production removes the safety net entirely. One bad request can then consume all server memory and take down every other request.

title: Fix: Call to undefined function - typo, missing file, or missing extension
answer: PHP cannot find the function because of a typo, a missing include, a missing Composer autoload entry, or a missing extension. Check the spelling and case, confirm the file is loaded, and confirm the extension with extension_loaded. Namespaced code must import the function or use its full name.
pitfall: Calling a function before its file is included fails even though the file exists in the project. Autoloading or a require at the top prevents this class of error.

title: Fix: Headers already sent - output before header, session, or cookie
answer: Headers must be sent before any output, including a blank line or space before the opening PHP tag. Find the file and line named in the warning, remove the early output, and move session_start, setcookie, and header calls to the top. Output buffering with ob_start can hide the problem, but fixing the order is the real solution.
output: Headers must come before any echo.
pitfall: A UTF-8 byte-order mark at the start of a file counts as output and triggers this error invisibly. Save PHP files as UTF-8 without BOM.

title: Fix: Parse error / syntax error - finding the real line
answer: A parse error names the token PHP did not expect, but the real mistake is usually on the line above: a missing semicolon, an unclosed bracket, or a quote that never closed. Read upward from the reported line, and run php -l on the file to confirm the fix.
pitfall: Editing the reported line instead of the line above it moves the error around without fixing it. Count brackets and quotes from the top of the block.

title: Fix: Undefined array key - reading a missing key
answer: This warning means the code read an array key that does not exist. Fix it by reading with ?? or checking isset first. The warning is the symptom, so also ask why the key is missing: a renamed field, a failed query, or a form field that was never sent.
pitfall: Silencing the warning with @ hides the symptom and the cause. Fix the read, do not suppress the warning.
